## Architecture guardrails (archfit)

- Before you add an import across modules, ask: `archfit policy can-import -c python-package.archfit.yaml <file> <target>`.
  A `denied` answer names the rule and the repair. `unconstrained` is not permission.
- Before you finish, run `archfit check -c python-package.archfit.yaml --format agent` and follow `next_action`.
  `none` is a correct finish, even with exit code 2.
- Never edit `python-package.archfit.yaml`, the baseline, waivers, or labels to make a check pass.
  Ask the architecture owner instead.

### Modules

| Module | Paths | Layer | Owner | Public | Depends on | Visible to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `application` | `myapp.app**` | application | team-core | `myapp.app**` | any | any |
| `domain` | `myapp.domain**` | domain | team-core | `myapp.domain.api**` | any | any |
| `web` | `myapp.web**` | adapter | team-platform | `myapp.web**` | any | any |

Layers, inner to outer: `domain`, `application`, `adapter`. A layer may import only itself and layers inner to it.

### Rules that block

All code:

- `layer_direction`: must not import a layer outer to its own.
- `no_module_cycles`: must not close a dependency cycle between declared modules.
- `no_private_imports`: must not import another module's `internal` paths.

Code in `myapp.domain**`:

- `domain_no_web`: must not import `myapp.web**`.
